input.quote: 14.2.2 At-Will Termination by PB. PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ. In the event that PB terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.2 then in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4, PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.
input.rationale: Both limbs of the rule fail the fallback. (1) Our convenience exit: Section 14.2.2 is the only at-will right we have and it is double-gated — unavailable until SFJ has paid or incurred $60 million of Development Costs and unavailable at all once the first Regulatory Approval is received — and its price is 300% of all Development Costs paid or incurred. In a multi-year term that is effectively no usable convenience right, and the exit charge is orders of magnitude beyond the fallback's cap of roughly three months' fees. (2) SFJ's exit: Sections 14.2.6 (Change of Control of PB) and 14.2.10 (JSC decision disagreement) each let SFJ "in its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement in its entirety at any time" with no stated notice period, and 14.2.3 permits immediate termination on a Material Adverse Event — a counterparty walk-away on fewer than 90 days' notice, which the playbook treats as walk-away territory. We proposed the fallback rather than the preferred position because the existing bargain is a development-financing structure in which SFJ funds the trials against Approval Payments, so a no-penalty 30-day exit would be disproportionate: instead we make PB's at-will right exercisable at any time on 90 days' notice, cut the exit payment to the 150% multiple SFJ itself already accepts in Sections 14.2.6 and 14.2.8.1, and impose a 90-day notice floor on SFJ's discretionary terminations. Related buy-out pricing under Section 6.7 is a payments term and is not flagged again here.

proposal.summary: Make PB's at-will exit genuinely available (90 days' notice, no $60M/pre-approval gate) with the exit payment reduced to 150% of Development Costs, and require 90 days' prior notice for SFJ's sole-discretion terminations.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our playbook requires a workable customer convenience exit and no vendor walk-away on short notice; as drafted PB can only exit after SFJ has spent $60 million and only by paying 300% of Development Costs, while SFJ may terminate in its sole discretion with no notice period. We have moved PB's at-will right to 90 days' notice without the spend gate, aligned the exit payment with the 150% multiple SFJ already uses in Sections 14.2.6 and 14.2.8.1, and required 90 days' prior written notice for SFJ's discretionary terminations.

ops.oldText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
ops.newText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to SFJ.

ops.oldText: SFJ may, in its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement in its entirety at any time following a Change of Control of PB that occurs prior to the date of payment by PB of the final Approval Payment.
ops.newText: SFJ may, in its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement in its entirety upon not less than ninety (90) days' prior written notice to PB at any time following a Change of Control of PB that occurs prior to the date of payment by PB of the final Approval Payment.
